key_insight: LLMs can reach the right diagnosis for the wrong reasons, showing evidence-value misalignment where confidence and diagnostic accuracy do not reliably reflect enough or the right evidence.
clinical_relevance: In medical decision support, this means a model may answer correctly while still being unsafe or premature, so evidence verification matters as much as accuracy.
method: Built MedEVM, a dynamic benchmark with 1,050 cases across 24 disease systems.
Tested 9 LLMs in a turn-by-turn setting where models had to wait for more evidence or submit a diagnosis.
Created EVD-Harness with offline diagnostic knowledge and online stages for observation management, witness verification, and submission control.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on 1,050 cases across 24 disease systems, and EVD-Harness improved accuracy by 12.0–51.1 percentage points across five LLMs.
watch_item: This is a benchmark and control framework, so real-world clinical deployment still needs careful validation, especially for noisy workflows and safety-critical use.
paper_title: Can LLMs Value the Right Evidence? Evidence-Value Misalignment in Dynamic Medical Diagnosis
